VEGF increases the permeability and fluid filtration of the parietal sheep pleura ex-vivo through VEGFR-2 stimulation.
vascular endothelial growth factor increases the permeability to proteins and water of sheep pleura through vascular endothelial growth receptor 2 stimulation.
vascular endothelial growth factor, a cytokine that is produced in large quantities in pleural effusions, increases the permeability to water of the sheep parietal pleura ex vivo.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of vascular endothelial growth factor in the development of the pleural effusion.
the role of Vascular endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) in the pathogenesis and pathophysiology of pleural effusion.
the study of the role of Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF) in the pathogenesis, treatment and prevention of pleural effusion.

VEGFR2 is expressed on sheep pleural mesothelial cells, VEGF increases pleural permeability through VEGFR-2 stimulation and this effect can be blocked by the VEGFR2 inhibitor DC101.
the VEGF increases the permeability to water of sheep pleura by activating VEGFR-2.
VEGF increases the permeability in sheep pleura ex-vivo through VEGFR-2 stimulation.

VEGF increases the permeability through the stimulation of its receptors VEGFR2 and VEGFR1.
VEGF increases the permeability to macromolecules of sheep pleura by stimulating VEGFR2.

pleural mesothelial cells express VEGFR2 and that VEGF induces an increase of pleural permeability through this receptor.
